Some studies reported statistically significant improvements, while others found no impact. 3. A number of studies included in the analysis were conducted exclusively in high-income countries (HICs), limiting the generalizability of the findings. 4. Over half of the studies had small sample sizes, which may reduce the reliability of the results. 5. For caregiver depressive symptoms, while no serious limitations were noted in some studies, the pooled estimates still showed a wide CI, reflecting imprecision. 6. In the domain of socioemotional development, several studies could not be included in meta-analyses due to a lack of statistical differences, and the pooled results had wide CIs. 7. Behavioral problems were assessed in multiple studies, but findings were mixed, with some studies reporting null impacts and others showing significant reductions in problem behaviors. 8. Attachment outcomes were evaluated in two randomized controlled trials (RCTs), both of which demonstrated positive impacts on attachment measures. 9. For height-for-age z-scores (HAZ), pooled results showed wide CIs, and some studies had small sample sizes, limiting the precision of the findings. 10. Caregiving practices were assessed in 18 RCTs, with some studies showing significant improvements, while others reported mixed or null effects. Differences in the magnitude and direction of effects were noted. 11. Caregiver-child interactions were evaluated in 12 RCTs, with no serious limitations in some studies, but the pooled estimates had wide CIs, indicating variability in the results. 12. Cognitive development was assessed in 52 RCTs, with positive effects observed in some studies and null effects in others. The pooled effect size had a wide CI, reflecting inconsistency. 13. Language development was evaluated in 10 RCTs, with some studies reporting no impacts and others showing positive effects. The pooled results had wide CIs, and some studies had small sample sizes. 14. Motor development was assessed in one RCT, which was conducted in an HIC. The study had serious limitations, and no pooled effect size was available. 15. Prosocial behavior and socioemotional development were evaluated in one RCT, which also had serious limitations and no pooled effect size. 16. Combined nutrition and caregiving interventions were compared to standard care in several studies. While some studies found positive impacts, others reported null or negative effects. The pooled effect size had wide CIs, and many studies had small sample sizes. 17. Weight-for-age z-scores (WAZ) were assessed in four RCTs, with two studies showing positive impacts and the others reporting no effects. The pooled results had wide CIs, and some studies had small sample sizes. 18. Self-efficacy was evaluated in three RCTs, with some studies reporting no effects and others showing mixed results. Data could not be meta-analyzed due to the lack of unadjusted means and standard deviations. 19. Caregiver mental health was assessed in four RCTs, with some studies reporting significant declines in depressive symptoms, while others found no effects. The pooled effect size had a relatively tight CI, but the studies were conducted in HICs, limiting generalizability. 20. Caregiver knowledge was evaluated in two RCTs, with one study reporting significant improvements and the other finding no effects. The sample size was adequate, but data could not be meta-analyzed. 21. Combined caregiving and nutrition interventions were compared to caregiving interventions alone. Some studies found positive effects, while others reported null or negative impacts. The pooled effect size had wide CIs, and many studies had small sample sizes. 22.
